Notes: Chosen for DAC (needed by memory experiment) + backup SRAM + hardware CRC32 + cheap dev board for parallel firmware work. F411 has no DAC - disqualified.

Keeps backup SRAM (reset log + error counters) alive through a full brownout.

Purpose: LC filter between 5V0 and the LDO input
Notes: v2 NEW and NOT optional. LDO PSRR collapses above ~100kHz-1MHz and the TPS63020 switches at ~2.4MHz, so the LDO alone will NOT remove switching ripple. 22uF each side of this puts the filter corner well below the switching frequency.
THE memory experiment. STM32 DAC drives the feedback node to sweep the rail and find the retention threshold.
Proves a bit error was not caused by a rail dip. Without this M7 is unfalsifiable.
Reads back the actual margined voltage and the memory leakage current (itself a temperature dataset).

X7R. Y5V loses most of its value at temperature extremes.

Purpose: Altitude and pressure - M1 M2 M3 M4
Notes: ONLY realistic part reaching stratospheric pressure. BMP390/BMP280/BME280 stop at 300 hPa = 9 km and are WRONG for this mission. Port must not be coated or blocked.

Description: 10-1200 mbar, same range as MS5611, different output coding
Notes: v2 NEW - the only part v2 adds. MS5611 is the independent variable for M1 M2 M3 and M4: one sensor, four missions. A DIFFERENT part number rather than a second MS5611 because two identical sensors from one reel share failure modes and calibration errors. Agreement between the two is meaningful evidence; disagreement tells you something real. Also gives a free cross-check dataset.
RH is only meaningful below ~10 km. Above that absolute humidity is ~0 and response time goes to hours. Also detects condensation/icing on descent - a real failure mode.
+/-0.1C matters: the memory retention curve is plotted against this axis.
THE M1 measurement. Works to -200C with no semiconductor to freeze out. This is what real radiosondes use. Mount OUTSIDE the insulation.
A resistive divider into the STM32 ADC will NOT give the accuracy M1 needs for comparison against ERA5.
The whole PT1000 accuracy chain sits on this resistor. 0.1% 25ppm minimum. Keep away from the regulators.
Cheap thermal map of the board. One near the regulators one near the memory group.

Description: GNSS module with integrated patch antenna
Purpose: Position altitude time wind - M1 M3 M4 M5
Notes: MUST set airborne <1g dynamic model (CFG-NAVSPG-DYNMODEL=8) over UBX AT EVERY BOOT or the fix stops at 18 km. Integrated patch removes an entire RF chain from the board. Route 1PPS to a timer input capture.
Best gyro noise in class. +/-32g and high ODR give burst and parachute-shock capture for free. Avoid MPU-6050 - obsolete and heavily counterfeited.

v2 CHANGE from MMC5983MA. MMC has better noise but LIS3MDL is an ST part stocked everywhere with drivers in every framework. Its job is spin rate and coarse heading for the M6 antenna-orientation analysis - LIS3MDL is far more accurate than that job needs. Trading unneeded performance for supply certainty on an optional part.

Three CALIBRATED channels. Cheap single-channel UV parts (GUVA-S12SD ML8511 VEML6075) cannot produce a defensible irradiance figure. NEEDS a quartz or PTFE window - ordinary plastic blocks UVB and UVC entirely.

VALID ONLY BELOW ~5 km. No published low-pressure spec; the fan and the mass-concentration algorithm both assume near-sea-level air density. Power it down above 6 km. This is where the public-health signal is anyway.
BUY IT - do not design a 400V flyback on your first PCB. SBM-20 is Soviet-surplus and common in the CIS. WARNING 400V DC on the module - keep it physically separate.
Only galvanic path from the HV module. A fault there cannot reach the MCU. 2mm creepage and a keep-out slot under the body.
Volatile - has a genuine measurable Vdd retention threshold that moves with temperature. The primary M7 subject.

v2 CHANGE from Fujitsu MB85RS2MT. Same capacity, interface, physics and role. Infineon FRAM has consistently better Mouser/DigiKey stock. Fujitsu stays as the named alternate - if it is in stock when you order, either is fine.
Floating-gate charge retention is strongly temperature dependent. CRITICAL because it is also your backup log if the SD card fails.

v2 CHANGE: footprint only, DO NOT POPULATE. Erratic stock, $26, and it is the least informative of the four technologies - it is the control expected to show nothing, and the SEU statistics already predict zero events in every device. Keep the SOIC-8 pads; solder one in if it turns up cheaply later.
Push-push not hinged - better vibration retention. Add a mechanical retainer or tape for flight.
Industrial grade -40C rated. Consumer cards are NOT specified below 0C. SD cards are a leading cause of lost balloon data - write a raw circular log not FAT and mirror to the W25Q128.
During the V_MEM hold phase the memory may sit at 1.2V while the MCU is at 3.3V. Hi-Z plus series limiting prevents ESD-structure injection and latch-up. Place at the MCU end.

v2 CHANGE from Delock 12592. 850-930MHz covers BOTH 868 and 915 in one part number - real insurance while the frequency ruling is pending. SX1262 is newer than SX1276 with lower RX current. Ebyte is the manufacturer selling direct, far wider stock than a German accessory brand. ~1/3 the price. NEVER key both radios at once - hard firmware interlock required. Pre-matched certified front end: you design only a 50 ohm trace to the U.FL.
Needs the 5V rail. Published "300mW max" does not resolve real TX current - MEASURE IT on arrival. NEVER key both radios at once - they will desense each other.
Matches the LR900-A supplied cable.
Keep it short. Every centimetre is loss at 868 MHz.
One per radio.
Dipole needs no ground plane and has predictable nulls (up at the balloon down at the ground) - neither points at your station. Hang it below the payload.
TX current is a step load. Without local isolation the rail dip shows up in M7 data as a false anomaly.
One per radio right at its supply pins.

v2 CHANGE from Samtec FTSH-105. Mechanically identical for a debug connector you will use ~50 times and that has nothing plugged into it in flight. Samtec is worth paying for on connectors seeing thousands of cycles or needing vibration retention - this is neither. Keep 2.54mm test points for SWDIO/SWCLK/NRST/GND as a fallback regardless.
Lets you extract flight data in the field without opening the sealed enclosure.
Keyed so it cannot be reversed. Label the silkscreen with the module-side voltage.

The most-touched connector on the board.
On every line that leaves the board: UART to radios PT1000 Geiger SD.
Plus a test point so you can force the bootloader during bring-up.
High impedance so add 100nF at the ADC pin and use a long ADC sampling time.
Visible through the enclosure or on a light pipe. Saves enormous time on the launch field.

Order 10x quantity. Assortment kit is cheaper than reels.
